subject: sociology
title: What is a Gender Role? Adventure
welcome_lead: Pink for girls, blue for boys? Says who? 🚹
meta_desc: Gender Roles Adventure 1 — KS3 Sociology on what gender roles are and where they come.
final_note: You learned what gender roles are and how socialisation creates them.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sex is biological — bodies.

Gender is social — what's seen as 'male', 'female' or other.

Gender roles are expected behaviours.

Stereotypes:

  • 'Boys don't cry.'
  • 'Girls love pink.'

These are taught — not natural.

We learn gender from:

  • Family clothes and toys.
  • School rules.
  • Media and adverts.
  • Friends.

Many roles are changing — more equal parenting, more women engineers. 👷‍♀️

mcqs.q: What are Weber's three dimensions of stratification?
options: Ethnography is the study of different ethnic groups only.
Weber's three dimensions are upper, middle and working class.
Class (economic position in markets), status (social honour/prestige), and party (organised power) — Weber argued these can vary independently, unlike Marx's economic-determinism view.
Weber agreed with Marx that class is purely economic.

mcqs.q: According to Becker, what makes an act deviant?
options: Breaking a law makes any act deviant.
Being labelled as deviant by others - deviance is in the reaction, not the act.
Ethnography is the study of different ethnic groups only.
Acts are objectively deviant regardless of context.
